curiosities: Its GamePad has its own screen, so a game can go on without the TV.
It plays Wii games and uses Wii Remotes.
About 13.5 million were sold, one of Nintendo's lowest totals.
Many of its games were later re-released on the Switch.
It launched in North America on 18 November 2012.
It was Nintendo's first console with high-definition video.
Its processor, Espresso, has three IBM PowerPC cores; its graphics chip, Latte, is AMD's.
The GamePad's screen is 6.2 inches and touch-sensitive, like the DS's.
Miiverse, the social network built into it, closed in November 2017.
Nintendo stopped making it in January 2017.
Its eShop stopped selling games in March 2023.
